Subject: Urgent: Possible exfiltration affecting NovusBank — notification/next steps

Hi Grace / Neha,

We detected anomalous outbound activity from a subset of sessions that appear to have touched data for a NovusBank integration (customer IDs redacted). Our SOC flagged potential exfiltration to an external bucket. We are treating this as a suspected data incident and wanted to confirm Redwood's notification obligations under the DPA and the practical handoff for forensic evidence.

Immediate asks:
- Please confirm whether Redwood considers this a security incident under Section 5 of our DPA and the contractual notification window you will use.
- What evidence can you preserve/export (logs, KV cache dumps, request metadata) and how will you transfer it to our SOC?
- Which subprocessors (if any) might need to be engaged or notified by Redwood?

We have a short window for internal escalation on our side and would appreciate an acknowledgement within 4 hours. If you require a secure channel for transfer, we can provide our SFTP endpoint or a Gouvern secure bucket—please advise required formats and a point of contact.

Thanks,
Alex Ramirez
Sr. Incident Manager, NovusBank
incident@novusbank.com

Alex — thanks for the heads-up and for the sample.

Acknowledged. We will treat this as a suspected incident for NovusBank while we confirm scope. Preliminary responses from Redwood:
- Acknowledgement: this message confirms receipt and that we're triaging.
- Initial notification timing: we will provide an initial written acknowledgement and high-level scope within 4 hours of this email, followed by an interim update within 48–72 hours, and a full incident report within 30 days where feasible (subject to investigative constraints and redaction needs).
- Evidence: our platform can preserve the following on request — request/response logs, KV cache id maps (redacted), GPU-local model-cache snapshots for relevant sessions. We typically produce a manifest (forensic_snapshot_manifest.txt) describing preserved artifacts and hashes.
- Transfer: preferred flow is (1) redacted logs first over an encrypted channel; (2) then secure transfer of full artifacts once an NDA/confidentiality addendum is in place if required by subprocessor or cross-border rules. We can push artifacts to your SFTP or to a governed bucket. See attached transfer_instructions.txt for our preferred ciphers and ports.

Neha (privacy/legal) and Kimberly (security) are looped for contractual/technical confirmation. Ben, can you confirm whether we need a written addendum before transferring raw log exports to a US-based third-party SOC?

--
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security & Trust | Redwood Inference

On Tue, May 4, 2027 at 9:44 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Neha (privacy/legal) and Kimberly (security) are looped for contractual/technical confirmation. Ben, can you confirm whether we need a written addendum before transferring raw log exports to a US-based third-party SOC?

Alex / team — quick legal note: under our standard DPA (Section 5, Notification & Cooperation), Redwood must notify "without undue delay" and provide reasonable cooperation to investigate. Practically, to avoid cross-border or subprocessor issues we suggest the following interim language for this thread while we work through formal paperwork: 

"Redwood will: (i) acknowledge suspected incidents to the affected controller within 4 hours of detection; (ii) provide an interim factual update within 72 hours; (iii) preserve and transfer forensic artifacts to Controller-designated recipients under an executed Transfer and Evidence Access Addendum or existing DPA terms; (iv) only involve subprocessors where necessary and after Controller approval for direct data handoff."

Two points to confirm:
1) Does NovusBank require Redwood to notify any named subprocessors directly? If so, list them (we currently use AWS, GCP, and an external logging provider).
2) For transfers of raw logs that may contain personal data, our Privacy team recommends either (A) redacted-only initial transfer until a limited-scope addendum is signed or (B) an explicit controller-provided authorization (email thread suffices for immediate transfers in urgent cases).

If Novus wants immediate raw exports to their SOC with no addendum, please confirm in writing and include the recipient's full organization name and contact info. Otherwise we'll proceed with redacted artifacts first.

Ben Carter
VP, Legal — Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: proposed_notification_text.txt
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 12:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Possible exfiltration affecting NovusBank — notification/next steps

Alex / team — technical runbook below. Short version: we can preserve and export; timeline depends on scope.

Planned technical actions (high level):
- Snapshot preservation: create immutable snapshots of affected instance(s) and capture process lists and network flow logs (T+0).
- Log export: generate redacted request/response log CSVs first (remove payloads/PII), deliver within 6–12 hours over SFTP with AES-256-GCM.
- Full artifacts: full raw logs, KV cache dumps, and model-cache files are larger and may require an approved transfer agreement. We estimate 12–48 hours to prepare after authorization.
- Subprocessor considerations: if data touched a third-party logging pipeline, we will need to coordinate with that vendor for raw log access (we will notify only with Controller approval).

Secure transfer parameters (also in transfer_instructions.txt):
- Preferred: your SFTP endpoint (supporting key-based auth) or our secure presigned-transfer to a governed bucket with 7-day expiry.
- For encrypted archives we will use: AES-256 + SHA256 manifest and provide a separate key exchange via OOB channel (Signal or designated KMS).

Evidence manifest (attached) contains file-level checksums, timestamps, and redaction notes. We will also provide a redacted log sample (redacted_log_sample.csv) so your SOC can verify relevance before raw handoff.

If Novus wants Redwood to trigger subprocessors directly, please confirm the exact subprocessors and provide controller authorization. We will not independently notify subprocessors without controller direction unless required by law.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Operations | Redwood Inference

- Provide SFTP details and recipient contact (secops-intake@novusbank.com) by EOD today.
- Confirm whether we want Redwood to contact the logging vendor directly — our privacy team prefers Redwood to coordinate initial requests with the vendor, so please stand by for a separate authorization email from our legal team.
